native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: In the Catalonia study region, the prevalence of non-native plant species introduced via the gardening pathway varies steeply by habitat — it is highest in low-elevation, anthropogenically disturbed habitats close to roads and human settlements, peaking in Wetlands (50.0% of plots, 95% bootstrap CI 34.2–65.8%), Urban (47.7% [35.4–60.0%]), Coastal (44.8% [27.6–62.1%]), and Riparian (36.1% [24.6–47.5%]), and falling to near-zero in Rock outcrops (0%), Scrublands (1.9% [0.0–4.7%]), and forest interiors (Broad-leaved 4.4%, Coniferous 6.5%). Hurdle-binomial odds-ratios relative to the Croplands baseline (20.7% prevalence [12.0–29.3%]) are 3.84× for Wetlands, 3.50× for Urban, 3.12× for Coastal and 2.17× for Riparian (all BH-FDR q≤0.05); forests and Scrublands drop to 0.07–0.27× odds. The environmental gradient consistent with the ornamental-escape mechanism is dominated by elevation (odds ratio 0.10 per SD increase in elevation, q=0.0008) and proximity to roads (OR 0.68 per SD increase in distance-to-road, q=0.043), with the urban-vs-cropland buffer context collapsing to a non-significant PC1 once elevation is controlled. Stacked-composition analysis shows that when non-native species do occur they are dominated by gardening origin in lowland habitats (53–100% of non-native richness in Wetlands / Coastal / Coniferous / Broad-leaved forests) but not in Urban (29.8% gardening, 68.9% unintentional) or Croplands (18.5% gardening, 76.9% unintentional) where unintentional escape remains the leading driver. A supplementary phylogenetic-distance analysis suggests pathway categories are phylogenetically clustered (Mantel-style K=0.957, p=0.004, B=5000 permutations over 81 matched tips), but this does not drive the habitat-level hypothesis.
native_result.WorkflowB: Step 0 — n.total semantics: row-wise check that n.total == n.gard + n.unint + n.agfo (passed in 632/632 rows, Case A, so share_d == dominance_d). Step 1 — per-habitat prevalence, conditional share, and abundance-weighted dominance with B=5000 nonparametric bootstrap CIs at the plot level (low-n habitats flagged with explicit CIs). Step 2 — hurdle model with Croplands as reference: (a) binomial (logit) presence model with BH-FDR over 9 habitat coefficients (LLR p ≈ 4e-27, pseudo-R²=0.243); (b) zero-truncated Poisson count model (manual scipy implementation over n.gard>0, n=117 plots) with paired Poisson GLM with HC1 robust SE as a stability fallback (dispersion=1.14, Poisson adequate). Step 3 — env correlates: VIF check on 7 env predictors; PCA1 collapse of (urban.2009.500m, cropland.2009.500m) imposed (Urban=+0.84, Cropland=-0.55, 54% var) per protocol even though the VIF for that pair was ~1; remaining elevation/temperature/rainfall collinearity documented but not collapsed beyond protocol. Logit-LM on z-scored env predictors + BH-FDR q=0.05 across 9 coefs; joint habitat+env regularized logit (alpha=0.1) due to singular Hessian at full MLE. Step 4 — figure/data exports as CSV (matplotlib unavailable); ASCII bar visualisations embedded in ANALYSIS_REPORT.md. Step 5 — phylogenetic signal: custom Newick parser (biopython unavailable), 81/81 tips matched; K-clustering Mantel-style surrogate for Pagel's λ. Lazy confirmations: temporal_trends_contingency_table NOT used.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening-origin non-native plant prevalence varies steeply among habitats, peaking in Wetlands, Urban, Coastal and Riparian habitats and falling to near-zero in Rock outcrops, Scrublands and forest interiors.
sub_hypo.context: 632 sampled plots in the Catalonia study region; prevalence defined as the proportion of plots with n.gard > 0; plot-level bootstrap confidence intervals use 5000 resamples.
sub_hypo.relations: Prevalence (95% bootstrap CI): Wetlands 50.0% (34.2–65.8%), Urban 47.7% (35.4–60.0%), Coastal 44.8% (27.6–62.1%), Riparian 36.1% (24.6–47.5%), Croplands 20.7% (12.0–29.3%), Rock outcrops 0%, Scrublands 1.9% (0.0–4.7%), Broad-leaved forests 4.4%, and Coniferous forests 6.5%. In the binomial presence component of the hurdle model, odds ratios relative to Croplands are 3.84 for Wetlands, 3.50 for Urban, 3.12 for Coastal and 2.17 for Riparian (all BH-FDR q≤0.05); forests and Scrublands have 0.07–0.27 times the odds.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening-origin non-native plants are most prevalent in low-elevation, anthropogenically disturbed habitats near roads and human settlements, consistent with an ornamental-escape mechanism.
sub_hypo.context: Sampled plots in the Catalonia study region; environmental logit analysis uses standardized predictors and BH-FDR correction.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening-origin presence decreases with elevation (OR 0.10 per SD increase, q=0.0008) and distance to roads (OR 0.68 per SD increase, q=0.043). The urban-versus-cropland 500 m buffer PC1, with loadings +0.84 for urban cover and −0.55 for cropland cover and 54% explained variance, is not significant once elevation is controlled.

sub_hypo.text: Where non-native plants occur, gardening-origin species dominate non-native richness in Wetlands, Coastal habitats, Coniferous forests and Broad-leaved forests, whereas unintentional introductions dominate Urban habitats and Croplands.
sub_hypo.context: Plots with non-native species in the Catalonia study region; conditional composition and abundance-weighted dominance are evaluated by habitat. The identity n.total = n.gard + n.unint + n.agfo holds in all 632 plots.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening-origin species account for 53–100% of non-native richness in Wetlands, Coastal habitats, Coniferous forests and Broad-leaved forests. Urban composition is 29.8% gardening and 68.9% unintentional; Croplands composition is 18.5% gardening and 76.9% unintentional.

sub_hypo.text: Introduction pathway categories show supplementary evidence of phylogenetic clustering, but this does not drive the habitat-level hypothesis.
sub_hypo.context: 81 matched plant phylogenetic tips; supplementary Mantel-style clustering analysis with 5000 permutations, used as a surrogate for Pagel's λ.
sub_hypo.relations: Introduction pathway categories are associated with phylogenetic relatedness, with Mantel-style K=0.957 and permutation p=0.004.
